## f7aca7ec2012

**Finding: reproduced sampler shortcut; target left unchanged.** The intended
legend selector is redundant in the audited production distribution. I scanned
6,000 deterministic draws: seeds 0..1999 in each of easy, medium, and hard, with
sample index `seed*17+3`. In 6,000/6,000 scenes the legend-selected component was
also the unique globally largest component; there were no ties, no larger
alternative, and no missing legend target. A rival can therefore ignore the
legend, select the globally largest component, crop it, and flip it.

The retained counterexample starts from canonical train pair 1 and removes the
later tied size-5 nonlegend component. It passes the audited generator's
`self_check` with no messages. The legend-selected target has size 4 while an
other-color object has size 5. Supported Racket execution returns the legend
object; the global-largest rival returns the other object, so the outputs differ.
This is a concrete in-validator-domain witness, not only a statistical
suspicion. Whether the validator is broader than the intended human domain is a
separate domain question.

Evidence: `checks/audit/f7aca7ec2012/evidence.json`, `input.json`, `racket.json`,
`rival.json`, and `construction.json`. Audited generator SHA-256 is
`a22315e26438c85b62730a50536d7eb02dc81561f788e584cb24a906d3115961`;
executed rule hash is `37a821ca77aa`. No source for this audit target was changed.

## f7aca7ec2012

**Reproduced shortcut on unchanged source; no audit-target files were edited.**
Current generator SHA-256 is
`a22315e26438c85b62730a50536d7eb02dc81561f788e584cb24a906d3115961`.
The generator always makes the legend-color target larger than every same-color
decoy and every other-color distractor. A rival can therefore ignore the legend
at `(0,0)`, select the unique globally largest nonzero component, crop it, and
flip it left-right.

An independent scan of seeds `0..499` in each of easy, medium, and hard, using
sample index `seed*17+3`, found the legend-selected object was also the unique
global largest object in **1,500/1,500** generated scenes; there were zero ties,
zero larger alternatives, and zero missing legend targets. This is a finite
scan, but it also follows directly from the current size bounds in source.

The exact retained counterexample in
`checks/audit/f7aca7ec2012/input.json` passes current `self_check` with `[]` but
breaks the equivalence: legend color 5 selects a size-4 object, while color 2 has
a size-5 object. Canonical Racket execution (rule hash `37a821ca77aa`) returns

```text
[[0,5],
 [5,5],
 [5,0]]
```

whereas the global-largest rival returns

```text
[[2,2],
 [2,2],
 [0,2]]
```

Evidence: `checks/audit/f7aca7ec2012/probe.py`, `probe.json`, `input.json`,
`rival.json`, and source-bound `racket.json`. The optional strict audit check
found no task-local/frozen tests and failed because no semantic contract is
declared; see `checks/audit/f7aca7ec2012-combined/`. This corroborates the
source-matched unresolved prior audit rather than certifying the whole domain.
